parts.title: Listening Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear Tasha talking to a friend about her family. What is each person's favourite thing?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Hi, Tasha. What's the matter?

script.speaker: Tasha
script.text: I've broken my dad's CD player and it's his favourite thing.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Wow! I didn't know people still used CD players!

script.speaker: Tasha
script.text: Dad does! My family is so old-fashioned. Mum has only just bought a <u>digital camera</u>. And now she likes it more than anything else. She uses my laptop to look at the photos!

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: But your sister has a laptop too! I suppose that's her favourite thing.

script.speaker: Tasha
script.text: Well, she plays games on it but I think she prefers the <u>TV</u>. She spends hours watching it.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Is your brother's tablet still his favourite thing?

script.speaker: Tasha
script.text: Now it's the <u>mobile</u> he got for his birthday.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: What did he do with the tablet?

script.speaker: Tasha
script.text: He gave it to our grandma so she could use the internet. Then she was given a <u>laptop</u>. She says that's her favourite thing because it's bigger. She speaks to my cousins in Australia on it.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Does your grandfather still borrow DVDs from the library?

script.speaker: Tasha
script.text: He doesn't need to. We taught him how to download films onto the <u>PC</u> that he never used before and now he says it's the best thing in the world!

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 2
parts.instructions: Read the three texts about computers and school. For each question, choose the correct answer.

persons.name: Berta
persons.text: We use computers and other technology in almost every class at school, and everybody is given a tablet computer to use. We also do ICT every Wednesday. Nobody buys textbooks any more, but we still read books from time to time. In the future, I don't think people will have to go to school. We'll have all our lessons online at home and that will give us more time to do sport with our friends.

persons.name: Elif
persons.text: We aren't taught ICT at our school. If we need to use the internet, the teacher takes us to the computer room, but we mostly use books in class. I don't mind that because I don't really like spending my time on computers or things like that. I prefer to finish my homework quickly and then go out skating with my friends. I'm sure that in the future people will use computers to study even more than now.

persons.name: Gloria
persons.text: We don't study ICT as a school subject because it's part of every class and we can go online in all the classrooms. I often use the internet to do my homework, too. My mum says we never use our school books but this isn't true. It's just that we use technology, too. I think the lessons of the future will be online, without books. But I hope we still go to school, because I might miss my friends if I have to study alone at home.

items.question: Who studies ICT as a school subject?
Who never uses school books during lessons?
Who does a sport with friends after school?
Who says schools won't use books in the future?
Who has to go to another classroom to go online?
Who likes studying with other people?

parts.title: Listening Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear Alice talking to her mum about the things people in her family want to find on the internet. What thing does each person want to find?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: It's very quiet, Alice.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: I know, Mum! Everyone's looking for something on the internet.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Even Dad?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Yes, he wants to download a <u>movie</u> – that one about the piano player.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Your brother wants to see that. What's he looking for?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: He's looking for an <u>electric guitar</u> – he wants to start learning before our holiday.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I'll ask your sister to help him. What's she trying to find?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: She's looking for a <u>printer</u> that'll work with her new tablet. … You know our cousin's here?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Really?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: She was looking for a better tablet, but couldn't find one she wanted. Now she's searching for a <u>digital camera</u> to take on holiday.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Aunt Jane will be pleased.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Yes, she phoned earlier. She's looking on the internet because she wants a <u>tablet</u> that she saw on TV. That's for their holiday, too, so she can download pictures from her camera.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Can't you take pictures with a tablet? By the way, you know Grandma's going with them?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Yes. She says she needs a <u>clock</u> to travel with, so she's looking at a website now, then she's going to watch TV.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Right!

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 2
parts.instructions: Read the three texts about the computer game competition. For each question, choose the correct answer.

persons.name: Charlotte
persons.text: I learned to make games at school in IT and art lessons when I was ten. We made video cartoons. I also worked on the game for this competition at school. Last year, my brother and I made a different game for a school competition, and we won a trip to a computer games company with one of the teachers. When I leave school, I'd love to work there, but I don't think I'll earn a lot.

persons.name: Abigail
persons.text: I made the game for fun for my brother. I planned to make a different one for the games competition. However, when I showed it to my IT teacher at school, he thought it was brilliant and said I should enter it! Everyone just loves playing it. I'm really excited about the competition, but don't think I'm going to win. In the future, I want to start my own technology company.

persons.name: Françoise
persons.text: When I was 11, I played video games all the time. So I began to check new video games for a computer games company. We had to play them and find any problems and I earned money for doing it. I also started to get ideas and I began to make the game I'm entering for the competition. I've always worked hard and I usually pass all my art, IT, business and maths exams at school easily. I hope to do a course in computer art at college next year.

items.question: Which person has already received a prize in a competition?
Which person is good at several subjects at school?
Which person wants to get a job with a computer games company?
Which person was given advice about the competition by someone at school?
Which person has made films during school time?
Which person was paid to check new computer games when she was younger?
Which person made a game for a member of her family?
